title: Claudius Gothicus II - Antoninianus - Divo Claudio - CONSECRATIO - Roman
description:
Roman Imperial Coin – Antoninianus of Claudius II Gothicus (Posthumous Issue)
 

 Roman Empire, AD 270


 Honored Emperor: Claudius II Gothicus
 

 Issuing Authority: Quintillus
 

 Reign period: AD 270
 

 Denomination: Antoninianus
 

 Mint: Mediolanum (modern Milan, Italy)
 

 Date: AD 270


 Composition: Silver (billon)
 

 Manufacture: Struck
 

 Diameter: approx. 17.3mm
 

 Weight: approx. 2.55g


 Obverse:
 

 Radiate and draped bust or radiate head of the deified Claudius II Gothicus, facing right. (Very well detailed on this coin)
 

 Legend: DIVO CLAVDIO
 

 Translation: To the Divine Claudius


 Reverse:
 

 Altar.
 

 Legend: CONSECRATIO
 

 Translation: Consecration
 

 Mint marks: Vary, including -/-//-, -/-//P, -/-//S, -/-//T, or -/-//Q


 References:
 

 RIC V, Claudius Gothicus, no. 261
 

 OCRE canonical URI:
 

  http://numismatics.org/ocre/id/ric.5.cg.261
 

 Historical note:
 

 This is a posthumous commemorative issue struck under Emperor Quintillus following the death and deification of Claudius II Gothicus. The CONSECRATIO reverse with altar symbolizes Claudius’ elevation to divine status by the Roman state.
